raw_response:
I will still do it much like last year, because changing too much is risky and fertilizer costs real money. On my 12.4 mu, I will keep wheat-maize on 10 mu, and I will keep 2.4 mu for stevia. I do what I have seen work around me in Quzhou. If a neighbor cuts fertilizer too hard and loses yield, that loss hurts more than wasting a little bag of fertilizer, so I would rather lean a bit heavy than too light. For wheat, I will put the base fertilizer in before sowing, give one topdressing at greening and watch the moisture; with well water, I can hold the stand steady. After wheat, I will put maize on the same 10 mu, use hybrid seed, keep the stand even, and give water at the key time before tasseling and during grain filling if the ground is dry. Stevia is the crop I will watch more closely, because leaf yield depends on keeping it fed and clean, so I will not let weeds and insects get ahead of me. I have some family working off-farm, so I will keep the plan simple and practical, with rotary tillage where it saves labor and enough pesticide rounds to avoid losing the crop.
